name: pixman (SSE2 and NEON bilinear scaled fast paths)
baseline: pixman general compositing path (the generic C implementation that handles any format and operator combination; the same path Cairo's image backend falls back to)
workload: Bilinear-filtered SRC compositing of a 2000x2000 a8r8g8b8 image to a8r8g8b8 with a scale factor close to 1x (commit-message microbenchmark, MPix/s), plus a cairo-perf-trace replay of the firefox-planet-gnome trace on the image backend.
claimed_speedup: Commit message of the SSE2 fast path: 'approximately 2x faster than pixman general compositing path'. Microbenchmark on an Intel Core i7 (x86-64): 70.48 MPix/s before, 165.38 MPix/s after (2.35x, derived from page data). cairo-perf-trace image firefox-planet-gnome: 12.566 before, 10.961 after (1.15x, derived from page data; the page gives these figures without a unit). The message also says single-pass processing without a temporary buffer accounts for about 15% and loop unrolling for about 20% of the speedup.
hardware: Intel Core i7 (x86-64), exact model and clock not stated
stars_or_usage: Compositing backend library behind Cairo's image backend and the X.org server (usage from general knowledge, not verified this session). Only GitHub mirrors were reachable: aseprite/pixman 12 stars, X11Libre/mirror.fdo.pixman 0 stars.
tradeoffs: Fast paths are per-architecture and chosen at run time: x86 MMX/SSE2/SSSE3, ARM NEON and A64 NEON, ARMv6 SIMD, MIPS DSPr2, POWER VMX, RISC-V RVV (added in the 0.46 series). Only format and operator combinations that have a registered fast path are accelerated; everything else drops to the general path. The environment variable PIXMAN_DISABLE (for example 'sse2 ssse3 mmx') turns implementations off, so the same binary can be timed with and without SIMD. The SSE2 bilinear path in this commit is deliberately naive (one pixel at a time, SRC only, three repeat modes), and part of its gain comes from restructuring the scanline loop (single pass without a temporary buffer), not only from SIMD.
caveats: Tier C: the evidence is first-party commit messages written by pixman developers (Siarhei Siamashka at Nokia, 2011). The CPU is given only as 'Intel Core i7', and compiler and flags are not stated. The microbenchmark tool is not named in the message; the tree has test/scaling-bench.c, which times pixman_image_composite over a range of scale ratios, and lowlevel-blt-bench gained -b (bilinear) and -n (nearest) scaling modes later (both read from the mirror's master). The baseline in 'before' is the general compositing path of 2011, and later changes such as the SSSE3 bilinear iterator may have narrowed or moved the gap, so these ratios are historical. Other fast-path-vs-general rows found, all from commit messages on the same mirror: ARM NEON bilinear scaled src_8888_8888 on a Cortex-A8, 6.70 to 44.27 MPix/s (commit 17feaa9c50bb8521b0366345efe181bd99754957); NEON src_8888_0565, Cortex-A8 r2p2 at 1 GHz with 32-bit LPDDR at 200 MHz, 6.56 to 61.65 MPix/s (2ee27e7d79637da9173ee1bf3423e5a81534ccb4); NEON src_0565_x888, same board, 3.39 to 36.82 MPix/s (29003c3befe2159396d181ef9ac1caaadcabf382). Those messages do not say that 'before' is the general C path; this is inferred from the diffs, which only add the fast-path table entry and the NEON scanline function. A newer RISC-V commit has a stricter protocol: rvv 'Add a8r8g8b8 bilinear affine fetch' (e1f49d9e6665ce354b90a189bf7bb5bbde9a1f20) reports SpacemiT K3, GCC 15.2.0, release build, affine-bench rotate 29.15 to 44.74 MPix/s and shear 0.25 36.46 to 60.75 MPix/s as medians of five interleaved runs, but its baseline is the previous tree, not a stated scalar C build, and the 'release build' flags are not spelled out, so it was not used as the primary row. No SSSE3 fast-path-vs-generic numbers were found: the SSSE3 bilinear iterator commit message could not be retrieved. The aarch64 NEON commit (eadb82866b0f6a326a61c36f60e5c2be8f7479af) points to freedesktop bug 94758 for its results, which was not opened. No independent third-party benchmark was found. The canonical gitlab.freedesktop.org host failed from this environment (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), as did lists.freedesktop.org; the repo URL is the one supplied by the assignment, and every page opened is a GitHub mirror (X11Libre/mirror.fdo.pixman, aseprite/pixman) or a raw patch copy (steev/efikamx). The last commit date and the MIT license come from the X11Libre mirror (a read-only CI mirror of the upstream repository) and its COPYING file; aseprite/pixman is stale (newest commit 2022-02-19).
found_via: seed-record pass: assignment lead for pixman (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/pixman/pixman, not reachable); WebSearch 'pixman lowlevel-blt-bench NEON fast path vs generic C performance MPix/s commit' led to the aseprite/pixman mirror and to the steev/efikamx copy of Siamashka's bilinear patch series, whose upstream commit hashes were then opened on github.com/X11Libre/mirror.fdo.pixman.
